title: DECODING TRUST: A Comprehensive Assessment of Trustworthiness in GPT Models
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive assessment of trustworthiness in GPT models, evaluating their performance on various trustworthiness perspectives, including toxicity, stereotype bias, adversarial robustness, out-of-distribution robustness, robustness on adversarial demonstrations, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content: Imagine you're having a conversation with a language model, and you ask it to generate a response. But, what if the model generates something toxic or biased? Toxicity and stereotype bias are just two of the many trustworthiness concerns in language models. In this paper, we'll explore these concerns and more, using real-world examples and benchmarks to evaluate the trustworthiness of GPT models.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: We designed a comprehensive evaluation framework to assess the trustworthiness of GPT models. Our framework includes eight trustworthiness perspectives, each with its own set of evaluation scenarios and metrics. For example, to evaluate toxicity, we used a combination of standard benchmarks and our own manually designed prompts.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: Our evaluation results show that GPT-4 outperforms GPT-3.5 on the standard AdvGLUE benchmark, with a score of 85.6% compared to 82.1%. However, GPT-4 is more vulnerable to adversarial attacks, with a success rate of 89.2% compared to 80.5% for GPT-3.5.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: The trustworthiness of language models has significant implications for their deployment in real-world applications. Biased or toxic responses can have serious consequences, such as perpetuating harmful stereotypes or offending users. Our evaluation framework provides a comprehensive assessment of trustworthiness, helping developers and users make informed decisions about language model deployment.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: Our evaluation framework introduces several key innovations, including the use of diverse system prompts to evaluate toxicity and bias, and the development of adversarial attacks to test the robustness of language models. These innovations provide a more comprehensive assessment of trustworthiness and help identify areas for improvement.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content: To try out our evaluation framework, visit our website and explore our dataset. You can also use our concise version of the paper as a starting point for your own trustworthiness evaluations.
